name: Fey Adept
role: Fey adepts are versatile casters and experts of trickery

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.description: A fey adept is proficient with all simple weapons.

features.name: Casting
features.description: A fey adept may combine spheres and talents to create magical effects. A fey adept is considered a High-Caster. (Note: All casters gain 2 bonus talents and a casting tradition the first time they gain the casting class feature.)

features.name: Spell Pool
features.description: A fey adept gains a small reservoir of energy he can call on to create truly wondrous effects, called a spell pool. This pool contains a number of spell points equal to his class level + his casting ability modifier (minimum 1). This pool replenishes once per day after roughly 8 hours of rest.

features.name: Magic Talents
features.description: A fey adept gains a magic talent every class level, according to Table: The Fey Adept.

features.name: Fey Magic
features.description: At 1st level the fey adept gains the Illusion sphere as a bonus magic talent.

features.name: Master Illusionist
features.description: Whenever the fey adept ceases to concentrate on an illusion he is maintaining through concentration, or if he decides not to maintain an illusion at all after its creation, it remains for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 his fey adept level (minimum 1) before disappearing.

features.name: Shadowstuff
features.description:
Fey adepts gain a limited ability to wield shadowstuff-the pure essence of shadows. With this power, the fey adept can affect the world around him with his illusions by weaving reality into the images.

The fey adept gains a pool of shadow points equal to his Charisma modifier + 1/2 his fey adept level (minimum 1) that refills when the fey adept regains all of their spell points. A fey adept may spend shadow points to create any of the following effects.

• Shadowmark

The fey adept may spend a shadow point to hurl pure shadowstuff at a target within his illusion range, weakening its body and making its mind more susceptible to the fey adept's magic. This requires a ranged touch attack. If successful, the target takes 1d6 damage and suffers a -1 penalty to Will saves against all the fey adept's sphere abilities for 1 minute. This damage improves by 1d6 for every odd level the fey adept possesses, to a maximum of 10d6 at 19th level. The Will penalty increases to -2 at 7th level, -3 at 13th level, and -4 at 19th level. This penalty does not stack with itself. This is considered an illusion (figment, shadow) effect from the Illusion sphere.

• Create Reality

At 6th level, the fey adept may spend shadow points in conjunction with creating an illusion with the Illusion sphere to weave reality into the illusion. This grants the illusion the [shadow] descriptor.

This follows all the usual rules for creating and maintaining illusions, except the illusion gains an additional benefit depending on what illusion is created. Many of these benefits improve at 12th and 18th levels. Illusions still must possess the appropriate (sensory) talents to be believed. When using an illusion to mimic an effect from another sphere the effect still counts as an Illusion sphere effect (such as when calculating caster level) and does not count as the alternate sphere for other purposes, such as when applying talents or feats based on those spheres.

In order to create reality, the fey adept must spend spell points as usual to create the illusion, plus 1 shadow point + 1 per spell point that would be required by the mimicked effect in question. This includes spell point costs to maintain a

features.name: Darkvision
features.description: At 2nd level, a fey adept gains darkvision 60 feet. If he already possesses darkvision with a range of 30 feet or more, the range increases by 30 feet.

features.name: Truesight
features.description:
Once per day at 4th level, a fey adept may grant himself the ability to see all things as they truly are to a range of 120 feet for 1 round per level. The fey adept sees through magical darkness, notices secret doors hidden by magic, sees the exact locations of creatures or objects under blur or displacement effects, sees invisible creatures or objects normally, succeeds at all saving throws against illusions and sees through them naturally, and sees the true form of polymorphed, changed, or transmuted things. The fey adept may use this ability an additional time per day for every 4 levels beyond 4th, to a maximum of 5 times at 20th level. This does not allow the target to see through mundane disguises, non-magical means of hiding things, fog, or other such effects.

This cannot be combined with other magic that enhances the senses, such as a crystal ball.

features.name: Hide in Plain Sight
features.description: At 10th level, a fey adept can use the Stealth skill even while being observed. As long as he is within 10 feet of an area of dim light, a fey adept can hide himself from view in the open without anything to actually hide behind. He cannot, however, hide in his own shadow.

features.name: See in Darkness
features.description: At 14th level, a fey adept can see perfectly in darkness of any kind, even magical darkness that normally impedes darkvision.

features.name: Feytouched
features.description: At 20th level, a fey adept is treated as a fey rather than as a humanoid (or whatever the fey adept's creature type was) for the purpose of spells and magical effects. He also gains DR 10/cold iron, and a +2 luck bonus on all saving throws.

features.name: Permanent Illusion
features.description: At level 20, the fey adept can make one of his illusions permanent. Only one illusion may be made permanent in this way at one time. If another illusion is designated as permanent, the previous permanent illusion ends.

archetypes.name: Auteur [CS]
archetypes.summary: Auteurs are especially adept at using illusions to influence others.

archetypes.name: Dreamtwister
archetypes.summary: Dreamtwisters are especially adept at slipping illusions into the minds of their enemies.

archetypes.name: Inspired Inventor [CS] [LG]
archetypes.summary: Inspired Inventors use the Tinker sphere to create illusion-inspired machines.

archetypes.name: Immersed [SM-]
archetypes.summary: Immersed indulge in illusions, trading their truesight for more skilled fabrication.

archetypes.name: Regisseur [SM-]
archetypes.summary: Forsaking a connection to some quasi-real underpinning of reality, regisseure (singular regisseur) study numerous theatrical techniques to distort perceptions of existence.

archetypes.name: Seelie Disciple
archetypes.summary: Seelie disciples are musically-inclined and capable of fascinating their targets.

archetypes.name: Sidhe Invoker
archetypes.summary: Sidhe invokers manipulate the plane of faerie instead of using shadowstuff.

archetypes.name: Skulk
archetypes.summary: Skulks are experts at using the Dark sphere to manipulate shade and shadows.

archetypes.name: Solipsist
archetypes.summary: Solipsists are excellent at modifying the abstract states of reality to their benefit.

archetypes.name: Unseelie Disciple
archetypes.summary: Unseelie disciples are capable of making sneak attacks and taking rogue talents.

archetypes.name: Word Witch
archetypes.summary: Word witches are experts with the Creation sphere and can speak words of creation to create effects.

archetypes.name: Wunderkind [WoP]
archetypes.summary: The Wunderkind is essentially a complete change to the Fey Adept's abilities, making it closer to an alternate class than an archetype. Their abilities focus on the manipulation of emotions and illusions.
